title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding pages of the 1981 Longue Marche manuscript). K is a field, X is a smooth K-variety, and D = ∪_{i∈I} D_i is a normal crossings divisor with complement U. L is the function field of U, \bar L is an algebraic closure, and \mathcal E^{\bar L}_{(-)} denotes the (tame) arithmetic fundamental groups with base points in \bar L. For x ∈ Supp D, \tilde O_x is the (strict) henselisation and \tilde U_x = Spec \tilde O_x ×_X U is the punctured local tubular neighbourhood. By Abhyankar's lemma (eq. (34)) there is an extension 1 → \hat T^{I(x)} → \mathcal E_{\tilde U_x} → Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x)) → 1, where I(x) = {i : x ∈ D_i} and T = T(\bar L^*) is the Tate module of roots of unity.

For a valuation ring V of L/K with center x, the decomposition group N_V = \mathcal E_{\tilde η} maps to \mathcal E_U. This map factors as (35): N_V → N_x := \mathcal E_{\tilde U_x} → \mathcal E_U, and the image of the second map is the decomposition group of x.

On this page he states two presumptions ('sous réserve de vérifications') about the two factors.

1°) \mathcal E_{\tilde U_x} → \mathcal E_U is injective. Equivalently, its geometric part I_x ≅ T^{I(x)} → Π_{U/K} is injective, i.e. local tame inertia at a point of D injects into the geometric fundamental group of U. The left margin notes that the inertia 'I_x' and the index set 'I' are different letters. A later right-margin note retracts the claim: it is 'visiblement faux' for card I(x) ≠ 1. He sees this by replacing X with X' obtained by blowing up a point of D. Then at the point E ∩ D_1' the local Z^2 is generated by γ_E and γ_{D_1}, but these coincide in π_1(U). He then suggests injectivity may still hold for a suitable compactification X ⊃ U.

2°) Suppose V is 'zero-dimensional', i.e. a closed point of the Zariski–Riemann space \ddot X_{L/K}, so that k(V) is algebraic over K. Then N_V → N_x is open (first written 'surjective'). Since N_V/I_V = \mathcal E_{k(V)} injects as an open subgroup into \mathcal E_{k(x)} = N_x/I_x, this is equivalent to the inertia map I_V → I_x = \hat T^{I(x)} being open, or even surjective.

Purpose (next page): the section conjecture of §2. For a section of \mathcal E_U → \mathcal E_K attached to a K-trivial valuation with residue field K, 1° and 2° would imply that the image of G_K normalises a subgroup Δ_x ≅ \hat T^{I(x)} of π_U. This subgroup is nontrivial exactly when the valuation has no center on U, i.e. the section is not a rational point. This is the 'cuspidal / points at infinity' part of the section conjecture.
errors: 1° as first stated is false in general, as Grothendieck himself notes in the margin. Blowing up a point of a single component D_1 gives a crossing point E ∩ D_1' where the two inertia generators become equal in π_1(U). For card I(x) = 1 it can also fail without hyperbolicity assumptions (e.g. U = A^1 ⊂ P^1, whose tame geometric π_1 is trivial).

2° appears false in general when card I(x) ≥ 2. Take D = {xy = 0} at the origin and V the valuation f ↦ ord_t f(t, φ(t)) with φ a transcendental power series, φ(0) = 0. This V has center the origin, residue field K (so it is a closed point of the Zariski–Riemann space) and value group Z. Its tame inertia is rank-one Hom(Γ_V, T) ≅ \hat T, mapping to \hat T^2 by (v(x), v(y)) = (1, ord φ). That map is neither open nor surjective. Openness needs the values v(t_i), i ∈ I(x), to be Q-linearly independent, as for Abhyankar valuations of maximal rational rank. Grothendieck's next-page remark that 2° is 'essentially trivial, whether the presumption turns out true or false' is consistent with this.

The parenthetical claim that k(V) is finite over k(x) is unjustified. A K-trivial valuation of a function field can have residue field an infinite algebraic extension of K (non-Abhyankar valuations). Only an injection of Galois groups (not necessarily onto an open subgroup) follows in general.

ideas.what: Local tame fundamental group of the punctured henselian neighbourhood of a normal crossings point is an extension of Gal(k(x)) by \hat T^{I(x)}
ideas.modern_name: Abhyankar's lemma / tame local fundamental group, decomposition and inertia at boundary points

ideas.what: Question whether inertia at a boundary point injects into the (geometric) fundamental group of U; counterexample via blowing up a point of D
ideas.modern_name: injectivity of cuspidal / divisorial inertia in anabelian (hyperbolic polycurve) settings
ideas.usually_credited_to: studied for curves classically; in higher dimension in work of Mochizuki, Hoshi and others (unsure of precise attribution)

ideas.what: Sections of π_1(U) → G_K attached to K-trivial valuations of the function field; cuspidal sections normalise a nontrivial boundary inertia group Δ_x ≅ \hat T^{I(x)}
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal sections / valuative (birational) approach to the section conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: section conjecture: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983); valuative approach: Koenigsmann, Pop, Stix
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); the Longue Marche manuscript itself (circulated)

ideas.what: Openness of the inertia map I_V → I_x for zero-dimensional points of the Zariski–Riemann space
ideas.modern_name: inertia of valuations vs. divisorial / log inertia (Abhyankar valuations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: valuation theory (Zariski, Abhyankar); used in Pop's birational anabelian work

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates (and retracts in the margin for card I(x) ≥ 2) a global question: for which normal crossings compactifications X ⊃ U of an anabelian U does the full local group \mathcal E_{\tilde U_x} inject into \mathcal E_U? He suggests this holds for a suitably chosen compactification, calling it a global and 'aucunement triviale' question.
missed.quote: C'est visiblement faux pour card I(x) ≠ 1 ... Mais ... X ⊃ U ... injectivité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Injectivity of higher-codimension boundary inertia in π_1 of higher-dimensional hyperbolic varieties is relevant to cuspidal sections in higher dimension. Whether a 'good compactification' criterion exists seems only partially addressed in the literature (unsure).

deep.surprise_reason: This is an exploratory working page in the well-known Longue Marche manuscript, reducing the cuspidal part of the section conjecture to two local/global inertia questions. One question Grothendieck refutes himself in the margin; the other appears false as stated (transcendental-arc valuations). The higher-dimensional boundary-inertia question is a modest open thread, not a hidden result.
transcription_corrections: Right margin: likely 'C'est visiblement faux pour card I(x) ≠ 1, comme on voit en prenant pour X' au lieu de X, X' déduit de X en faisant éclater un pt de D ... Mais il est vraisemblable que pour X ⊃ U convenable, et ... injectif'.
Left margin: 'Les deux lettres I ne sont pas les mêmes' (inertia I_x vs index set I) is correct.
'\ddot X_{L/K}' presumably denotes the Zariski–Riemann space of L/K; 'de dim zéro' means V is a closed point.
In 2°, 'surjectif' is struck and replaced by 'ouvert'. At the bottom, 'est ouverte' is struck and the final word reads 'surjective', with a hesitant clause '– sans doute ...' partly struck.
